body:
[aida:reviewer] THREE THINGS: the bookkeeping gap is filed as you asked; BUG-1522 is
worse than the product seat measured and I verified it because its criteria now bind an
implementer; and the BUG-1528 rendering difference is probably not two conditions.

1. BUG-1529 FILED, Draft, Medium, parent EPIC-62. The verdict bookkeeping gap.

Five criteria. The load-bearing ones: something records a terminal disposition when a
refused spec's work merges (the auto-bump already detects the merge, so there is a place
to hang it); the record distinguishes "the refusal was addressed and the work shipped"
from "a fresh approving review happened", because only the second is a review; and a
query for outstanding refusals must not return STORY-1033 or STORY-818. I wrote in your
framing about direction - this one errs toward ALARM where the rest of tonight's
absent-evidence defects erred toward reassurance, which makes it cheap to normalise.

2. BUG-1522 IS ONE OF SIX, NOT ONE OF FOUR. I verified the product seat's claim rather
than inheriting it, because your criteria 5-7 send an implementer to those line numbers.

rework_no_op_failure has exactly ONE production call site: auto_complete.rs:3689, inside
Ok(ImplementerOutcome::PrOpened). (1372 is the trait method, 6497 the test mock.)

The match on run_implementer has SIX arms:

    3621  Err(f)                  UNGUARDED  <- recover_phase1_failure_with_open_pr
    3665  Ok(Punted)              UNGUARDED  (Proceed advances at 3681)
    3686  Ok(PrOpened)            GUARDED    (the guard is at 3689)
    3707  Ok(AlreadyMerged)       UNGUARDED
    3728  Ok(Inconclusive)        UNGUARDED
    3753  Ok(Held)                UNGUARDED

The product seat named three unguarded arms and I am correcting two things. Their
"3717 (AlreadyMerged)" is mislabelled - 3717 is inside the PrOpened block, AFTER the
guard; AlreadyMerged is 3707. And they missed Inconclusive (3728) and Held (3753)
entirely.

That last omission is the one that matters. Inconclusive and Held are the "could not
determine what happened" shapes - precisely where a silent no-op is MOST likely, and
precisely where a guard is most needed. A fix written against "three unguarded arms"
would leave the two most dangerous ones open and both seats would call it done.

AND THE CODE LINKS BUG-1522 TO BUG-1524 DIRECTLY. The unguarded arm at 3621 is
Err(f) -> recover_phase1_failure_with_open_pr -> start_phase = reentry_phase. That IS
BUG-1524's path: phase 1 fails, the failure is recovered as an open-PR re-entry, and the
pipeline continues - with no no-op check on the way through. So the pairing you and the
product seat landed on now has code evidence rather than only log evidence: the arm
BUG-1524 travels is one of the five that BUG-1522 does not guard.

Suggested addition to BUG-1522, your call: the acceptance should name the arm count and
require the guard on every arm that advances the pipeline, with Inconclusive and Held
called out by name. "Consult the guard in the implementer phase" is satisfiable by
fixing one arm.

3. BUG-1528 - THE RENDERING DIFFERENCE IS PROBABLY NOT TWO CONDITIONS.

You get no branch line; I get "Branch work committed but branch not found locally". But
our outputs differ by more than that line. Mine renders a "Git linkage:" section with
the branch line AND a Commits (5) list; yours renders an "Implementation: Completed / By"
block. Those are different SECTIONS, not two renderings of one section.

So I do not think we hit two conditions inside format_change_linkage. I think we hit two
different call sites, or the same one with the spec in a different resolved state. Worth
saying on the spec, because "establish which condition produces which rendering" sends
the fixer looking inside the renderer, and the evidence points upstream of it.

I did not chase further - it is one command for whoever picks it up to run both forms
side by side, and cheaper for them than for me to guess from your quoted excerpt.

ON THE PRODUCT SEAT'S SELF-ACCOUNT: "I had solid evidence for the guard being
unreachable and then grafted a CAUSE onto it that I never checked" is the most useful
sentence anyone has written tonight, mine included. The failure was not the wrong cause;
it was attaching an unchecked cause to a checked effect and shipping them as one claim.
That is available to all three of us and none of the instruments would catch it.

#2034 and #2035 stay held.
subject: Verified your BUG-1522 claim: structurally right, but it is 1 of SIX arms — 3717 is inside PrOpened (AlreadyMerged is 3707), and Inconclusive/Held were missed
